questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Rowlatt Act, which was introduced by the British government to curb political dissent in India?

options.text: Arrest of political leaders without warrants

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Restrictions on freedom of expression**__.

__
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**, officially known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, was enacted by the British government in India to suppress political dissent and revolutionary activities.
 
• It allowed the government to arrest individuals suspected of revolutionary activities without providing a warrant and detain them without trial for an indefinite period, which was a direct violation of basic human rights.
 
• One of the provisions included the **censorship of the press**, aimed at curbing the dissemination of anti-government information and revolutionary ideas.
 
• The act gave authorities the power to arrest political leaders and activists without requiring a warrant, which undermined legal safeguards for individuals.
 
• The provision of **"arrest without trial"** was one of the most controversial aspects, as it denied individuals the right to a fair trial, violating the principles of justice.
 
• However, the act did not explicitly include any clause that imposed **"restrictions on freedom of expression"**. Although censorship of the press indirectly affected freedom of expression, the act did not target this right specifically as a provision.
 
• This act faced widespread protests across India, including the famous **Jallianwala Bagh massacre**, which occurred as a result of public agitation against the act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Censorship of press**__

 __
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** imposed censorship on the press to suppress revolutionary ideas and anti-government sentiments.
 
• Under this provision, newspapers and publications were monitored, and any content deemed inflammatory or against British rule was censored.
 
• This restriction was aimed at controlling public opinion and preventing the spread of nationalist ideas.
 
 
 
• **Arrest of political leaders without warrants**__
 __
 
• One of the most criticized provisions of the **Rowlatt Act** was the authority given to the police to arrest political leaders and activists without requiring a warrant.
 
• This provision enabled arbitrary arrests, targeting prominent leaders involved in the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Arrest without trial**__
 
 
• The act allowed detention without trial, meaning individuals could be imprisoned indefinitely without being formally charged or given a chance to defend themselves in court.
 
• This provision violated fundamental judicial principles and sparked widespread outrage among Indians.

questions.question: Which force acts without physical contact and governs celestial body motion in mechanics?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gravitational Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Force** is a fundamental force that acts without physical contact.
 
• It governs the motion of **celestial bodies** such as planets, stars, and moons.
 
• This force is responsible for holding objects in their **orbits**, such as the Earth revolving around the Sun or the Moon orbiting the Earth.
 
• The force is described by **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**, which states that every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• Gravitational force is always **attractive** and acts along the line connecting the centers of two masses.
 
• It plays a critical role in the formation and structure of **galaxies, solar systems, and the universe itself**.
 
• Gravitational force also governs phenomena such as **tides**, which are caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun on Earth's oceans.
 
• It is one of the weakest forces in nature but has an infinite range, making it significant on a **cosmic scale**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Spring Force**__

 __
 
• **Spring Force** is a contact force that occurs in objects like springs when they are stretched or compressed.
 
• The force exerted by a spring is governed by **Hooke's Law**, which states that the force is proportional to the displacement.
 
• This force is used in various applications, such as **shock absorbers**, mechanical clocks, and measuring devices like **spring balances**.
 
 
 
• **Friction**__
 __
 
• **Friction** is a contact force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
 
• It is critical in everyday activities like walking, driving, and holding objects.
 
• However, friction cannot act at a distance and is not responsible for celestial body motion.
 
 
 
• **Tension**__
 
 
• **Tension** is a force that arises in strings, ropes, or cables when they are pulled taut.
 
• This is a contact force and is commonly seen in structures like **bridges** or when lifting objects using ropes.
 
• It does not act at a distance and is not involved in the motion of celestial bodies.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why removing all desktop icons does NOT impact the functionality of the applications in Windows OS?

options.text: Desktop icons are system-critical files required to run applications.
Windows OS duplicates all application files in the desktop directory.
Desktop icons are only visual shortcuts and not the actual application files.
The desktop is a virtual memory area where applications run in the background.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Desktop icons are only visual shortcuts and not the actual application files.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Desktop icons** represent **shortcuts** to applications, files, or folders. They are essentially links to the actual application files stored elsewhere on the computer, such as in the **"Program Files" directory** or other system locations.
 
• Removing or deleting desktop icons does not affect the underlying application files or their **functionality**. The applications can still be accessed via the **Start Menu**, Taskbar, or their installation directories.
 
• The desktop in the Windows operating system serves as a user-friendly area for quick access but does not store the actual programs or files.
 
• Even if desktop icons are removed, users can utilize other navigation methods, such as the **Windows Search functionality**, to locate and run applications.

questions.question: Why is the common cold rarely considered a lower respiratory tract infection?

options.text: The virus is destroyed in the alveoli.
It requires a vector for lower tract transmission.

Antibodies prevent it from entering the lungs.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rhinoviruses only infect the upper respiratory tract**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rhinoviruses** are the primary cause of the common cold and are responsible for more than 50% of cases.
 
• These viruses preferentially infect the **upper respiratory tract**, such as the nasal passages and throat.
 
• The upper respiratory tract provides a more suitable environment for rhinoviruses because of its **lower temperature (about 33°C)**, which is optimal for their replication.
 
• The lower respiratory tract, including the lungs and alveoli, generally has a **higher temperature** (around 37°C), which is less conducive for rhinovirus survival and replication.
 
• Rhinoviruses lack mechanisms to effectively invade deeper tissues like the lungs or lower respiratory tract.
 
• Infections caused by rhinoviruses are typically mild and self-limiting, targeting the **mucosal surfaces of the upper respiratory tract**.
 
• Other viruses, such as influenza or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), are more likely to cause lower respiratory tract infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **The virus is destroyed in the alveoli**__

 __
 
• The alveoli are small air sacs in the lungs that are involved in oxygen exchange. While certain viruses may struggle to survive in this environment, this is not the primary reason the common cold is rarely a lower respiratory tract infection.
 
• Rhinoviruses do not typically reach the alveoli due to their preference for the upper respiratory tract.
 
 
 
• **It requires a vector for lower tract transmission**__
 __
 
• Rhinoviruses are transmitted via **direct contact**, airborne droplets, or contaminated surfaces, not through a vector like mosquitoes or ticks.
 
• Vector transmission is more commonly associated with diseases like malaria or dengue.
 
 
 
• **Antibodies prevent it from entering the lungs**__
 
 
• While the immune system, including **antibodies**, plays a role in combating infections, the inability of rhinoviruses to infect the lower respiratory tract is primarily due to environmental and biological factors, not antibody interference.
 
• Antibodies are produced as part of the body's response to infection and do not specifically block rhinoviruses from entering the lungs.

• **A disagreement between Punjab and Haryana over territorial boundaries**__

questions.question: Which of the following physical factors influences the compactness of rural settlements in dry regions like Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Availability of water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Availability of water** is the most crucial factor influencing the **compactness of rural settlements** in dry regions like Rajasthan.
 
• In arid and semi-arid regions, **water is a scarce resource**, and its presence determines human settlement patterns.
 
• Villages tend to develop in a more **compact form** near water sources to ensure proximity and accessibility.
 
• Rajasthan faces extreme water scarcity due to its **desert climate** and low annual rainfall; thus, settlements often form around **oases, wells, or tanks**.
 
• Compact settlements help reduce the effort and time required to fetch water and allow better community management of water resources.
 
• Historically, people have relied on **stepwells (baolis), tanks, and rainwater harvesting structures** to meet their water needs, further influencing settlement patterns.
 
• In comparison, areas with abundant water sources generally feature dispersed settlements due to reduced dependency on a single water source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Groundwater salinity**__

 __
 
• Groundwater salinity refers to the **presence of high salt content** in groundwater, which can render it unsuitable for drinking or irrigation.
 
• While groundwater salinity is an issue in Rajasthan due to its geological conditions, it does not directly influence the **compactness of rural settlements**.
 
• However, it may determine the **location of settlements** by pushing people to areas with better water quality.
 
 
 
• **Soil fertility**__
 __
 
• Soil fertility refers to the ability of soil to support **plant growth** by providing essential nutrients.
 
• While it is a crucial factor for agricultural settlements, it primarily influences **land use and cropping patterns**, rather than the compactness of settlements.
 
• In Rajasthan, due to the sandy and infertile soil, settlements are often concentrated near water sources rather than fertile lands.
 
 
 
• **Altitude**__
 
 
• Altitude refers to the **height of a location** above sea level.
 
• While altitude can influence settlement patterns in hilly or mountainous regions, it is not a significant factor in the **flat terrain of Rajasthan**.
 
• In Rajasthan, the focus is more on water availability due to its **arid climatic conditions**.

questions.question: Which river is associated with the Mohenjo-daro site?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Mohenjo-daro** is one of the most prominent urban centers of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, which flourished around 2500 BCE.
 
• The site is located along the banks of the **Indus River** in present-day **Sindh province, Pakistan**.
 
• The **Indus River** played a crucial role in the development of the civilization due to its **fertile plains** and the availability of water for agriculture.
 
• Mohenjo-daro is famous for its well-planned city layout, which included **grid-pattern streets, drainage systems, and advanced water storage facilities**.
 
• The site is also home to the **Great Bath**, which is considered one of the earliest examples of public water architecture.
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, often referred to as the **Harappan Civilization**, is known for its advanced urban planning, trade systems, and cultural developments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Saraswati River**__

 __
 
• The **Saraswati River** is often mentioned in ancient Indian texts such as the **Rigveda**.
 
• It is believed to have been a major river during the Vedic period but is now considered a **lost river**.
 
• Some historians and scientists associate the Saraswati River with the **Ghaggar-Hakra River system**.
 
• While the Saraswati River has significance in Indian mythology, there is no concrete evidence linking it to Mohenjo-daro.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River**__
 __
 
• The **Ganga River** is one of the most sacred rivers in India and is associated with the **Gangetic Plain**.
 
• It is geographically located far from the Indus Valley Civilization sites and is not linked to Mohenjo-daro.
 
• The Ganga River basin was central to the development of later civilizations in India, such as the **Magadha and Maurya empires**.
 
 
 
• **Yamuna River**__
 
 
• The **Yamuna River** is a major tributary of the Ganga River.
 
• It flows through northern India, including prominent cities like **Delhi, Agra, and Mathura**.
 
• The Yamuna River is not geographically connected to the Indus Valley Civilization or Mohenjo-daro.

questions.question: How many national waterways have been declared for development under the National Waterways Act, 2016?

• Under the **National Waterways Act, 2016**, a total of **111 national waterways** were declared for development.
 
• These waterways span across various **states in India** and are aimed at promoting **inland water transport** as a cost-effective and environmentally friendly mode of transportation.
 
• The act consolidated and replaced five existing Acts that covered only five national waterways, thereby aiming to create a unified legal framework for all waterways.
 
• The development of these waterways is managed by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**, which oversees their maintenance and utilization.
 
• The National Waterways include major rivers such as the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, and Mahanadi**, and their tributaries, along with canals and backwaters.
 
• Waterways are considered a critical part of the **Sagarmala Project**, which is aimed at enhancing the logistics capabilities of India.
 
• National Waterway 1 (NW-1), stretching along the **Ganga River** between Haldia and Allahabad, is one of the most significant waterways in India.
 
• The development of these waterways supports **trade, tourism, and regional connectivity**, contributing to economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **National Waterways Act, 2016** was enacted to utilize India's vast network of rivers, canals, and backwaters for transportation and trade.
 
• **National Waterway 2 (NW-2)** runs along the Brahmaputra River between Dhubri and Sadiya in Assam.
 
• The **National Waterway 3 (NW-3)** includes the Kerala backwaters, spanning Kollam to Kottapuram.
 
• Waterway development aligns with the government's focus on **sustainable transportation** and reduction of road and rail congestion.
 
• India's inland waterways provide an opportunity to develop low-cost and efficient **cargo transport networks**.

questions.question: In the case of 'Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay vs Union of India (November 2024)', the Supreme Court dismissed a plea related to:

options.text: reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS) in jobs and education
Uniform Civil Code for all Indian citizens
constitutional validity of adding ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ to the Preamble
validity of Article 370 and special constitutional provisions

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**constitutional validity of adding ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ to the Preamble**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The inclusion of the words **‘socialist’** and **‘secular’** in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution was done through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976.**
 
• The term **‘socialist’** reflects the commitment of the state toward reducing inequalities in income, status, and opportunities.
 
• The term **‘secular’** denotes that India has no state religion and ensures freedom of religion for all individuals.
 
• The Preamble serves as the **guiding philosophy** and **objective of the Constitution.**
 
• The Supreme Court, in the case of **‘Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay vs Union of India (November 2024),’** dismissed the plea challenging the constitutional validity of adding these two terms to the Preamble.
 
• The court upheld that the inclusion of these terms aligns with the **basic structure doctrine** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The basic structure doctrine ensures that certain fundamental features of the Constitution cannot be amended or altered by the Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS)**__

 __
 
• The provision for **EWS reservation** was introduced by the **103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019.**
 
• It provides a **10% reservation** in educational institutions and government jobs for economically weaker sections of society.
 
• This reservation is applicable to individuals not covered under other categories like SC/ST/OBC.
 
• The criteria for EWS reservation include factors such as **annual family income** and **ownership of property.**
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)**__
 __
 
• The **Uniform Civil Code** seeks to replace personal laws based on religion with a common set governing matters like **marriage, divorce, adoption, and inheritance.**
 
• UCC is mentioned under **Article 44** of the Constitution as a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• The implementation of UCC remains a debated issue due to concerns over religious freedom and diversity.
 
 
 
• **Validity of Article 370**__
 
 
• **Article 370** granted special status to the state of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It was abrogated on **August 5, 2019,** effectively removing Jammu and Kashmir's autonomy under the Indian Constitution.
 
• The abrogation led to the bifurcation of the state into **two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.**
 
• The move was justified by the government as a step toward **national integration and development.**

questions.question: Where are files and folders typically stored in a computer?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hard Drive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Hard Drive** is the primary storage device in most computers where files and folders are typically stored.
 
• It is a non-volatile storage device, meaning that it retains data even when the computer is turned off.
 
• Hard drives use **magnetic storage technology** to store and retrieve digital data.
 
• They are used to store the operating system, software applications, multimedia files, documents, and other data.
 
• Hard drives can be of different types, such as **HDD (Hard Disk Drive)** or **SSD (Solid-State Drive)**, where SSDs are faster and more reliable.
 
• Modern hard drives come in various storage capacities ranging from **500 GB** to several **terabytes (TB)**, depending on the user's needs.
 
• Hard drives are connected to the computer's motherboard using **SATA, NVMe, or IDE interfaces**.
 
• They are integral to data storage in personal computers, servers, and other computing devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monitor**__

 __
 
• A **Monitor** is an output device used to display visual information from a computer.
 
• It does not store files or folders; it only shows information processed by the computer.
 
• Monitors are available in various types, such as **LCD, LED, and OLED**, offering different resolutions and display technologies.
 
 
 
• **Printer**__
 __
 
• A **Printer** is a peripheral device used to create physical copies (hard copies) of digital files.
 
• It is not used for storage; its purpose is to output data onto paper or other media.
 
• Printers can be classified into types like **inkjet, laser, and dot matrix printers**, depending on the technology they use.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard**__
 
 
• A **Keyboard** is an input device that allows users to type and interact with a computer.
 
• It is not a storage device; it is designed for entering data and commands.
 
• Keyboards come in various formats, including **mechanical, membrane, wireless, and ergonomic designs**.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts allowed the Crown to take over governance from the East India Company?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** was enacted in the aftermath of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, which exposed the administrative inefficiencies of the East India Company in governing India.
 
• This Act marked the beginning of direct control of India by the **British Crown**, ending the rule of the **East India Company**.
 
• The Act provided for the appointment of a new post of **Secretary of State for India**, who was responsible for overseeing India on behalf of the Crown.
 
• The governance structure established under this Act included the formation of a **Council of India**, which acted as an advisory body to the Secretary of State.
 
• The Act vested all powers, territories, and revenues of the East India Company in the hands of the **British Queen**, thereby consolidating imperial authority.
 
• This transition was officially proclaimed by **Queen Victoria in 1858**, emphasizing the Crown’s commitment to justice, equality, and non-interference in religious matters.
 
• The Act also aimed to improve the administrative efficiency of India and ensure better coordination between the British Government and Indian administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Charter Act, 1813**__

 __
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** renewed the East India Company’s charter for 20 years but ended its monopoly on trade with India.
 
• The Act allowed **Christian missionaries** to propagate their religion in India.
 
• This Act marked the beginning of the British Government’s financial responsibility for the administration of India.
 
 
 
• **Ilbert Bill, 1883**__
 __
 
• The **Ilbert Bill** was introduced by **Viceroy Lord Ripon** to allow Indian judges to try British offenders in criminal cases.
 
• It faced strong opposition from the European community in India, leading to significant political controversy.
 
• The controversy around the Bill highlighted racial discrimination in colonial India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1861**__
 
 
• The **Indian Councils Act, 1861** marked the beginning of the legislative devolution process in India by involving Indians in the legislative process.
 
• It restored the power of the **legislative councils** at the provincial level, allowing them to make laws.
 
• The Act also introduced the practice of **non-official members** in the legislative councils.

questions.question: What is the longitudinal extent of India?

__
 
• The **longitudinal extent of India** lies between **68°7'E** and **97°25'E**.
 
• This longitudinal spread covers a distance of approximately **2,933 km** from west to east.
 
• The longitudinal extent influences the **time zone** of India, with the country following the Indian Standard Time (IST), which is based on the **82°30'E longitude**.
 
• This geographical extent has a significant impact on the **climatic variations**, as well as the **sunrise and sunset timings** across the eastern and western parts of the country.
 
• The easternmost point of India is located near **Kibithu in Arunachal Pradesh**, while the westernmost point is near **Ghuar Mota in Gujarat**.
 
• The vast longitudinal extent also means that India has a diverse range of **landforms, climates, and ecosystems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Standard Time (IST)**__

 __
 
• IST is the time observed throughout India, calculated based on the **82°30'E longitude**.
 
• It is **5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of GMT (Greenwich Mean Time)**.
 
• IST helps maintain a uniform time system across the country, despite the vast longitudinal extent.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Longitudinal Extent**__
 
 
• The longitudinal extent results in a time lag of about **2 hours** between the easternmost and westernmost parts of India.
 
• For example, the sun rises in **Arunachal Pradesh (easternmost state)** much earlier than in **Gujarat (westernmost state)**.

questions.question: Which moderate leader, often referred to as the 'Grand Old Man of India,' became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons and helped shape the early nationalist movement?

• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was a prominent moderate leader and is often referred to as the '**Grand Old Man of India**'.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the **British House of Commons** in 1892 as a member of the Liberal Party.
 
• He played a critical role in shaping the **early nationalist movement** in India.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji authored the famous book "**Poverty and Un-British Rule in India**", where he highlighted the economic drain caused by British rule.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress** in 1885, which later became the leading organization in India's independence movement.
 
• Naoroji was instrumental in articulating the idea of **Swaraj (self-rule)**, laying the groundwork for future freedom struggles.
 
• He advocated for Indian representation and rights in British administration and worked tirelessly to raise awareness about India's plight in Britain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rash Behari Ghosh**__

 __
 
• **Rash Behari Ghosh** was an Indian lawyer, politician, and philanthropist.
 
• He served as the **President of the Indian National Congress** in 1907 and 1908.
 
• He was known for his moderate political stance and contributions to social reforms.
 
 
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__
 __
 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was another prominent moderate leader and the founder of the **Servants of India Society**.
 
• He was a mentor to **Mahatma Gandhi** and emphasized constitutional reforms and non-violent methods.
 
• He played a significant role in advocating for Indian self-rule through gradual reforms.
 
 
 
• **Pherozeshah Mehta**__
 
 
• **Pherozeshah Mehta** was a distinguished lawyer and politician from Bombay.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its President in 1890.
 
• He was nicknamed the "**Lion of Bombay**" for his leadership and contributions to Indian politics.
